task.title: Preparing the YAML configuration file by using the CLI
task.shortdesc: To prepare your proof of concept Red Hat Quay deployment for launch, you can create a config.yaml file with database, Redis, and storage settings and copy it to your configuration directory. You can use the CLI to build the configuration bundle that the registry container reads at startup.

step.cmd: Enter the following command to create a minimal config.yaml file that is used to deploy the Red Hat Quay container:
Copy and paste the following YAML configuration into the config.yaml file:

info.codeblock: BUILDLOGS_REDIS: host: quay-server.example.com password: strongpassword port: 6379 CREATE_NAMESPACE_ON_PUSH: true DATABASE_SECRET_KEY: a8c2744b-7004-4af2-bcee-e417e7bdd235 DB_URI: postgresql://quayuser:quaypass@quay-server.example.com:5432/quay DISTRIBUTED_STORAGE_CONFIG: default: - LocalStorage - storage_path: /datastorage/registry DISTRIBUTED_STORAGE_DEFAULT_LOCATIONS: [] DISTRIBUTED_STORAGE_PREFERENCE: - default FEATURE_MAILING: false SECRET_KEY: e9bd34f4-900c-436a-979e-7530e5d74ac8 SERVER_HOSTNAME: quay-server.example.com SETUP_COMPLETE: true USER_EVENTS_REDIS: host: quay-server.example.com password: strongpassword port: 6379
